item.title: Inde Navarrette Cast As Rogue: Ex-streamer lands MCU’s new X-Men role; Obsession paved the way
item.description: Inde Navarrette’s career has reached a major milestone after she was cast as Rogue in Marvel’s upcoming X-Men reboot. The actress first gained recognition through roles in 13 Reasons Why and Superman & Lois before earning critical praise for her intense performance in Obsession. Her journey also includes a past as a Twitch and YouTube streamer. Now, Navarrette is stepping onto Marvel’s biggest stage as one of its iconic mutants.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: In 1953, Emma tried hiking the Appalachian Trail, got lost and was rescued; two years later...
item.description: Emma Gatewood etched her name in history in 1955 as the first woman to conquer the Appalachian Trail solo at the remarkable age of 67. With minimal equipment, she bravely journeyed over 2,190 miles, transforming the narrative around long-distance hiking for women. Her perseverance and spirit culminated in two additional hikes, serving as an inspiration for countless adventurers seeking freedom and adventure.

item.title: In 1933, Lincoln's Crooked House was marked for demolition; work revealed a hidden...
item.description: In the midst of a demolition in 1933, builders stumbled upon a remarkable 16th-century timber-framed structure known as the Wonky House. This architectural gem narrowly evaded obliteration and has since undergone conservation efforts to rectify damage caused by death-watch beetles and previous poor repairs. Thanks to significant funding, extensive restoration will soon provide unique holiday accommodations and community spaces, welcoming visitors to enjoy its rich history.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 8-year-old boy catches a piranha while fishing with dad at Pennsylvania lake
item.description: While fishing near Philadelphia, an eight-year-old boy made an unusual catch: a piranha. Officials identified this tropical fish as non-native to Pennsylvania, raising alarms over the potential dangers of exotic pets being set free into local waters. Releasing such species is illegal and can jeopardize public safety. Following their unexpected encounter, the boy and his father took responsible action to humanely dispose of the piranha.

item.title: A Maine oyster farm is testing a floating conveyor that moves oyster baskets through water and air
item.description: Engineers in Maine are developing an innovative solar-powered floating system tailored for oyster farming. This unique platform incorporates a vertical conveyor that efficiently transports oyster baskets from underwater to above, aiming to enhance production while significantly lessening the labor demands on farmers. Additionally, it aids in shaping the oysters and cleaning their shells from unwanted marine growth.

item.title: Got a secret you can’t tell anyone? Visit this ‘grave of secrets’
item.description: A unique art installation in Brooklyn offers a place for visitors to anonymously share their deepest secrets. French artist Sophie Calle created a marble obelisk where people can deposit written confessions. This project, which began in 2017, will continue until the year 2042. Secrets deposited will be exhumed and cremated in a ceremonial service periodically. The installation provides a moment of catharsis and a chance for reflective unburdening.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: San Diego student develops red-light therapy to help heal wounds in space
item.description: An 18-year-old San Diego student has been named a finalist in the 2026 Regeneron Science Talent Search for developing a low-cost red-light treatment to improve wound healing in microgravity. Leanne Fan built a $200 device to simulate microgravity and found that the treatment accelerated tissue regeneration in flatworms by 95.2%. Tests with human cells also showed faster cell movement during wound closure.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Virginia re-wet a swamp across 150 miles of old ditches; peat traps 200,000 tonnes of carbon
item.description: North Carolina is restoring its coastal peatlands by bringing water back to areas damaged by drainage, farming and timber activities. The projects aim to reduce the risk of severe peat fires while keeping carbon stored in wet soils. At Pocosin Lakes National Wildlife Refuge, 37,000 acres have been restored, with water-control structures helping recreate natural water movement. Similar work at Angola Bay Game Land is restoring ditched peatland and wetland habitat. The efforts also support wildlife, improve resilience to flooding and sea-level rise, and involve local communities and landowners in managing water across the coastal landscape.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Connor Hill, 17-year-old Pennsylvania student who wrote a computer program to...
item.description: Connor Hill triumphed in the competition with his exceptional algorithm for classifying noble polyhedra, discovering two infinite families alongside 146 distinct shapes. Edward Kang's AI tool for autism screening claimed the second position, and Iris Shen's innovative blood cancer research involving clams took third place. Additionally, Regeneron expressed their commitment by extending sponsorship for another ten years, ensuring continued support for emerging scientific talent.

item.title: China launches 24th batch of low-orbit internet satellites from Hainan site
item.description: The launch took place from the southern island province of Hainan, which has become an important location for China's commercial space activities. The latest mission is part of China's ongoing effort to build large networks of low-orbit satellites that can provide internet connectivity from space. The rocket lifted off at 12.10 pm Beijing time and successfully placed the satellites into their designated orbits.

item.title: Mississippi’s termite swarms are here: A single treatment can cost up to $1,750
item.description: Termite swarms in Mississippi signal developing colonies that require prompt homeowner attention and professional inspection. Eastern subterranean termites swarm from winter into early summer, while Formosan termites appear later. Spotting swarmers indoors strongly indicates an active infestation needing immediate professional treatment. Preventive measures and early intervention significantly reduce costly structural damage from termites. Homeowners should recognize signs and consult licensed professionals for effective termite control.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Hawaiʻi’s eucalyptus forests could help build the islands’ future
item.description: Hawaii's heavy reliance on imported building lumber may soon change, thanks to promising research into local eucalyptus. Scientists are evaluating the strength and durability of this homegrown resource to establish engineering design values necessary for structural uses. By successfully validating these traits, this initiative aims to lessen dependence on foreign materials and invigorate local industries, ensuring that communities' construction needs are met sustainably.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A 13-year-old crawled into a Tennessee cave and found a hidden lake
item.description: In 1905, a 13-year-old boy stumbled upon America's largest underground lake in Craighead Caverns, Tennessee. This expansive chamber, referred to as the Lost Sea, showcases traces of Indigenous habitation and mining activities from the Civil War. Nowadays, visitors have the opportunity to navigate the vast cavern and embark on a captivating boat ride over the hidden waters. The total size of this geological marvel continues to spark intrigue and investigation.
